To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a novel approach to growing deep neural networks over the course of their training, driven by principled combinations of accuracy and sparsification objectives, that is able to start with a small, simple network and dynamically grow and prunes both layers and filters, and that we demonstrate that this method can produce compact networks with high accuracy, and drastically reduces the computational expense of network training.
our method is capable of producing compact, pruned neural networks with high accuracy and that this is done while drastically reducing the computational cost of training.
we develop a method for training deep networks that can grow and prune both filters and layers during the course of training.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: How can we train deep neural networks in a more efficient manner?
the following questions: How can we grow deep networks over the course of their training?

the following questions: How do we train a deep neural network to grow in a structured and sparse way, starting with a small seed architecture and ending with a large, efficient architecture? How do we train this network in such a way that it can be used for inference, without any dedicated fine tuning stage?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our method can start training with a small, simple architecture and grow to a larger, more complex network, all while maintaining the same accuracy.
our approach is the best method for pruning deep neural network architectures.
we present an efficient and principled approach for growing and pruning networks during training.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
\textbf{We develop an approach for training efficient deep networks, which can start from a simple seed architecture and grow and prune the network during training.
we can train a network with the same accuracy as ResNet-50, but with 47% fewer parameters, and 47% fewer training and inference FLOPs.

we develop a novel approach that combines the benefits of pruning, architecture search, and continuous relaxation, while being able to train and prune in a unified manner, and without any fine-tuning.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to train large networks in a more data-efficient way by dynamically growing and pruning them during the training.

it is possible to grow deep networks efficiently by a combination of accuracy and structure objectives, and that the resulting networks can be more efficient than those found through dedicated pruning or search methods.
we can train more efficient networks by growing them during training, and that we can do this without any fine-tuning.
